utterances.text: That we will not be able to be a part of these task forces if our detectives are being drawn into things that violate city law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: They know that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And I think, in my experience, it is very important to the federal incentive structure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: agencies that the NYPD be in these task forces that we not pull out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So for the detectives to know that if they...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: They want us there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Are doing things they're not supposed to be doing, the consequences for them and their careers will be severe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And I think they actually want to be careful not to put themselves in a position where we are pulling out of a task force.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: It's also being very clear with the task forces from the federal side.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: They know that we will not be able to be a part of these task forces if our detectives are being drawn into things that violate city law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: That's one part.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: A second part as to your question about the sharing of information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: There really are two different categories, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: They know that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So one is a situation in which there's some criminal case that our detectives are working on with federal agents as part of a task force.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And I think, in my experience, it is very important to the federal

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Let's say they're investigating a federal murder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: There will be a free-flowing sharing of information in connection with that murder investigation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: That's what it means to do an investigation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: They're sharing a lesson.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: It's a partnership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: That's what it is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Now, they do not have direct access to our systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: No system at all?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: No federal agency has any direct access to NYPD systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: They do not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: But I want to be very clear with you that in connection with these cases that we are working on ourselves with our federal partners, we do share information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And it's not, and just, Councilmember, to your question, it's not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: In those situations, we're not thinking of it in terms of discrete pieces.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: In other words, you're asking about LPRs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: We're sharing information relevant to the investigation, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: I mean, the model and the task.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: force, right, is detectives working side by side with special agents, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So NYPD detectives working with an FBI agent to investigate, let's say, some murder, federal murder, let's say a murder for hire, which is, you know, federal murder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: There is going to be a sharing of information with them in partnership to help solve that murder together.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Now, to the extent we're talking about requests for information, and this is whether it comes into the real-time crime center or it comes into a task force or anywhere else,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: we have put in place, and again, this comes out of the DOI report, right, and questions and, you know,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: comes out of the DOI report and other things in terms of, okay, how are those requests being processed?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And one of our policies that I mentioned earlier is just about this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: For those types of requests, where do they go?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: How are they channeled?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: To the extent they're coming from a federal agency that is part of one of the task forces, it will be channeled through the task force.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Otherwise, it will go to the real-time crime center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: What ends up happening, though, is you have documentation requirements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: There are forms they have to fill out, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: The requesting agent, nature of the case, various things you can imagine, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And there's a level of vetting that goes on on the uniform side, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: But then, as part of the policy, for all the complications of the policy, everything ends up in the same place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: legal has to review before information is shared.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So myself or some of my colleagues, frankly, multiple times a day, we're reviewing these forms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And look, I will tell you, there are times when this is easy and straightforward and it's obvious that it's totally fine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: There are times when we need more information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And we will write back internally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: We'll be like, you have to go back to whoever it is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And by the way, it's not just even federal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: We get requests from other state agencies, other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And by the way, we have across the board rules.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So we're going to have the same rule if it's some state agency or municipality that we know never works with ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: There are some that sometimes do things with ICE in other jurisdictions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Same rule for everybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: We're vetting it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: If it's unclear what it's for, if it's not clear for us that it's criminal, if we have concerns that somehow this is going to go into immigration enforcement, in some context, we're asking for more information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: We're saying a lesson until we get more information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And there are times where we are not satisfied with the answers, and we write back, disapproved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And that's it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: I think it is a good, it is a, I'm very proud of what we put in place here.

chapters.summary: Avilés asks whether any request for NYC-owned data within a task force is vetted through an official form and legal review. Gerber says that process applies to requests unrelated to an NYPD case.
chapters.title: Avilés seeks clarity on vetting within task forces

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Okay, so I'm glad to hear that there is that amount of vetting going on.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: So I just want to be clear what you're saying is that any...

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Within the task force, any request for data that is housed in any one of

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: I will say New York City owned data infrastructure, which would be the anything, is getting vetted.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: It's going through an official request form that legal is then taking a look at.

chapters.summary: Gerber says when NYPD detectives work a case with federal agents, information sharing is not vetted by legal because it is part of the investigation. He says the risk is in external requests where NYPD is not on the case, which go through legal review.
chapters.title: Gerber distinguishes case-related sharing from external requests

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: If it's unrelated to a case we're involved in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Again, that's a bifurcation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So everything I'm describing, which is a very thorough, lengthy process, is for anything, any requests that are coming in, unrelated to an NYPD case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: If it's a case that we're on, we are not going through that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: That's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So again, in a situation when you have an NYPD detective on a task force working with an FBI agent to investigate a murder for hire,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: That partnership involves the sharing of information that is not being vetted by legal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: That is a detective and a special agent doing their job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And we cannot, I don't think it would work functionally at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: You know, if you have a...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: A detective and a special agent working together to solve a case, every time they're sharing information back and forth, legal's not vetting that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: But I think the critical point, though, is in those cases, the detective knows what it's for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: It's his or her case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: It's their case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Like, they're sharing information relevant to the murder case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: They know a special agent's asking for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: The concern, the risk, is in that whole universe of cases where it's not our case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: The question is, you know, what are we sharing for?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And that's where we have this very significant and rightly time intensive review process.

chapters.summary: Avilés says even case-related sharing is concerning because federal agents may be pursuing deportation. She asks NYPD to provide the council with a list of all task forces, their purposes, federal agencies, agent allocations, and information-sharing agreements.
chapters.title: Avilés raises concerns about federal deportation agenda; requests task force list

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: I think the concern is, even if it's your case, that there are other agents and a federal government hell bent.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: On chasing, detaining, and deporting non-citizens.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: That is what our concern is about.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: And it's a blurry line from our perspective, but for the record, because I know my time is up and the chair has been very, very gracious.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Can you provide to the council the list of all the task forces,

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: what their purpose is, what federal agencies sit on those task forces, how many agents are allocated to each one of those task forces, and what, if any, information share agreements are?

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Have been put together for each of those.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Yeah, I certainly will take that back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: We can provide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: I have to go through each of the categories of data you just gave.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: But yes, we can provide data to the council.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether the administration knew Floyd Bennett Field was being used for ICE training. MOIA says it learned through news reports and is disturbed that federal property is being used for such operations.
chapters.title: Chair asks about Floyd Bennett Field ICE training

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Did the administration know that the Floyd Bennett field was being used for ice training?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So, oh, you want to speak to that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember, we were not aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: We were made aware, at least Moya was made aware through the news reports and are very disturbed by the news that a federal property, this is federal property,

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: is being utilized for operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: You know, I'll say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Just point blank that our position is that no training for a rogue agency and a lawless agency like ICE is going to improve any of their conditions.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks how new protocols will manifest in possible anti-ICE protests at Floyd Bennett Field. Gerber says protest response is not based on the subject matter of the protest.
chapters.title: Chair asks about police response to anti-ICE protests at Floyd Bennett

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And in terms of police resources in case of a anti-ICE protest at Floyd Bennett Field,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: because of these reports.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: How are these new protocols and procedures, do you think, going to manifest itself in those ICE protests, anti-ICE protests happening, possibly happening?

chapters.summary: Gerber says NYPD facilitates First Amendment activity regardless of the protest's subject. He describes a 90-day rollout of a new Office of Community Safety civilian team and a new FAST team within Community Affairs.
chapters.title: Gerber says protest response not based on subject; new FAST team

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So when we're responding to protests and, frankly, acting to facilitate First Amendment activity, it's not dependent on the subject matter of the protest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So, Chair, you asked about sort of anti-ICE protests, but I wouldn't distinguish between anti-ICE or anti-something else, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: It's not based, it's actually very important that it not be based on the substance of the protest, the subject of the protest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So what the mayor and police commissioner recently announced, right, is not kicking in immediately.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: It's a 90-day window.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And I think, I mean, obviously, even now, we're bound by the protest settlement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: We have policies in place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: I think where you're going to see differences is, I mentioned this earlier, two parts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: One, ultimately, the Office of Community Safety and their civilian team, and that's going to take long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: for them to roll out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: But ultimately, as I understand it, I don't want to speak for the Office of Community Safety, but ultimately, they're going to have a civilian team in dialogue with protesters, a dedicated team doing that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Within our Community Affairs Bureau, there will be a new, this will be within 90 days, a new team, FAST, right,

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: where within Community Affairs, officers really who are devoted to and focused on that dialogue with protesters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: So certainly in those respects, at least, you're going to see a shift in terms of the dedicated teams, both NYPD and then Office of Community Safety.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación thanks the administration panel and notes DOC is not present. She says she will ask DOC-related questions for the record and allow MOIA or NYPD to answer if they can.
chapters.title: Chair thanks administration and turns to DOC questions

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I want to thank you both for being here, all three of you, but both entities for being here.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I know DOC is not here.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: One of these bills is in relation to DOC.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And so I am going to ask questions of...

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: DOC, who I would have asked these questions to, to put on record.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: If by any chance either one of your entities could answer any of these questions, I'll be looking for the green bulb to go on and I will allow you to answer on their behalf.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I'm imagining that there may not be a lot of opportunity to do that, but I do want to get it on the record in terms of these questions and of the bill that is proposed.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks about DOC's EO 13 email audit. MOIA says the audit is supposed to be completed by the end of the year.
chapters.title: Chair asks about DOC email audit under EO 13

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: So under EO 13, DOC is reportedly working with their IT team to set up an audit of emails.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Can DOC or anyone here share an update on this audit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: That audit is supposed to be completed by the end of the year.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks how frequently DOC notifies ICE of upcoming release dates without a judicial warrant. MOIA says such incidents should be reported under Local Law 228 and defers operational details to DOC.
chapters.title: Chair asks DOC about notifying ICE without judicial warrant

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: This is starting off good.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: In terms of having answers.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Proposed intro 1078A limits communication between DOC and federal immigration authorities.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: How frequently does the DOC notify ICE of individuals'upcoming release date when ICE has not presented a judicial warrant?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I'm going to say that any of those incidents should be reported under local law 228.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: If not, if there's anything more specific, defer to the Department of Corrections.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And what does the notification process look like?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: What is the difference between notification and transfer?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: On the operational side, I would defer to the Department of Corrections.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks what operational barriers prevent DOC from banning communication and transfers without a judge-signed warrant. MOIA says it cannot answer and notes EO 13 includes training but lacks specifics.
chapters.title: Chair asks about operational barriers and warrant training

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Speaking of which, what operational barriers, if any, prevent DOC from adapting a rule banning communication and transfers without a judge-signed warrant?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: We wouldn't be able to answer that.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: How does DOC leadership communicate to DOC staff members the difference between an administrative warrant and a judicial warrant, and is this done regularly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I can say that part of the work that we've laid out on the EL-13 is that there is training in connecting to this, but I don't have more specifics.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación notes these bills were heard years ago under a different administration and hopes for different responses. She asks how DOC deals with ICE's reduced training and hiring standards.
chapters.title: Chair notes bills previously heard and asks about DOC policies

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And I just want to say also, you know, these two bills were heard prior under a different sponsor many years ago under a different administration with a different commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And so the reason why I think it's important for me to ask these questions and hopefully get something in writing and response is because I'm assuming that this is a very different response that I will, I'm hoping, right, that I would get a very different response to these questions

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: than we did in years prior.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: But just to put that on record.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The next question is, how does DOC deal with the realities that ICE has slashed?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: the training that it provides to new officers, and significantly lowered hiring standards since the start of its mass deportation agenda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember, we would defer these questions to our colleagues at DOC.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: As a DOC reviewed Intro 1077A, would the department support creating a clear rule?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: As this bill would do, understand what the answer would be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: The answer is the same, correct.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether DOC agrees sanctuary laws make New Yorkers safer and asks about Admin Code 9-131-B. She asks how DOC determines qualifying convictions and interprets the statute.
chapters.title: Chair asks DOC about sanctuary laws and detainer statute

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Does the DOC agree that the city's sanctuary laws make New Yorkers more safe?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Does the current DOC detainer law, admin code 9-131B, state that DOC may not honor a detainer by holding a person beyond time when such person would otherwise be released from the department's custody?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Or by notifying federal immigration authorities of such person's releases?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Can you explain why the agency believes that this section of the law overrides the clear prohibition on responding to warrantless detainers?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: With respect to violent or serious crimes expectations to the laws, the admin code says a person shall not be considered to have been convicted of a violent or serious crime unless the person has had a judgment entered against him or her on a violent

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: or serious crime within five years prior to the date of instant arrest.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: How does DOC determine whether someone has a qualifying conviction?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Does the DOC evaluate?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The offense for which the person is currently in custody?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And if so, how does the department interpret that to be in compliance with the statute?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And the last, well, it's not the last question, nevermind.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether there is a fusion sensor on Rikers Island and how DOC tracks compliance with detainer law. MOIA says it would have prepared answers if it knew, and defers to DOC.
chapters.title: Chair asks about Rikers fusion sensor and DOC compliance tracking

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Is there a fusion sensor on Rikers Island?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I mean, Chair, I would say that I know that if we would have been aware in regards to just some of the line of questioning connected to the Department of Corrections, we would have obviously, as we've done in the past with other agencies that we don't represent,

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: have been fully tried to provide you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't believe you for not knowing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you for saying that at the top, too.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: No, this is totally just for the record, but if you happen to know, you can say.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Is NYC currently opted into any threads functionality that permits information to be shared with access with securest customers?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I think we did speak about that a little bit earlier or it was brought up.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: How does DOC track compliance with the detainer law?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And beyond administrative discipline, what accountability mechanisms does DOC currently have in place?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And I will end it there.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación thanks the administration for staying through the hearing and acknowledges the pain in testimony. She says the council must tighten sanctuary laws and uphold them beyond press conferences.
chapters.title: Chair thanks administration and closes agency portion

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Again, I sincerely thank you all for being here for this whole time and hearing all of the questions.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I think, you know, Commissioner, you said it well.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: There's pain in some of the voices that we've heard today, and there's much more pain from community voices that we hear every day, the stories that we're hearing, seeing for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And, you know, our role and our job is to make sure that these laws are really tightening up.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The word sanctuary, right?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: That we're not just sprinkling that in press conferences or whenever it's politically, you know, good for us, but that we are actually upholding opportunities to strengthen them and to make them work for our communities.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And so I'm very glad to hear that the NYPD is in support of both of the bills.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I am very glad to hear that you are on your way there through the legal process and through the legislative process.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I am sure we can get there together and really on behalf of the constituents that we all serve.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: So thank you again for showing.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And we are going to be moving to the public testimony portion.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I am going to take a quick break.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I know we should all stand up, stretch a little, and we'll be back in about five minutes or so.

chapters.summary: Council staff ask attendees to take conversations outside and maintain decorum. They also announce that the overflow room is closing and later ask everyone to find their seats as the hearing resumes.
chapters.title: Staff manages break and room logistics

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, would you kindly please take all conversations outside?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We need to maintain decorum here.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Keep the volume down.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, if you have any belongings currently in the overflow room, please go grab them right now.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We're about to close that room up.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, would you kindly find your seats?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: The hearing is about to resume.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación resumes the hearing and opens public testimony. She explains decorum rules, the two-minute speaking limit, and how to submit written testimony.
chapters.title: Chair resumes and gives public testimony instructions

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I've got my coffee and I'm ready to go for the next round of this.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I am now opening the hearing for public testimony.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I remind members of the public that this is a government proceeding and that decorum shall be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: As such, members of the public shall remain silent.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: At all times.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who wish to testify.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: No video recording or photography is allowed from the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Further, members of the public may not present audio or video recordings as testimony, but may submit transcripts of such recordings to the Sergeant at Arms for inclusion in the hearing record.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: If you wish to speak at today's hearing, please fill out one of these appearance cards with the sergeant at arms and wait to be recognized.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: When recognized, you will have two minutes to speak on today's oversight topic, the current state of immigration enforcement activity in New York City, or on the legislation on today's agenda, including introductions 739, 1077A,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: and 1078A, and Resolution 729.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: If you have a written statement or additional written testimony you wish to submit for the record, please provide a copy of that testimony to the sergeant at arms.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: You may also email.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: written testimony to testimony at council.nyc.gov within 72 hours of the close of this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Audio and video recordings will not be accepted.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: For in-person panelists, please come up to the table once your name has been called.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Now I will call our first in-person panel.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación calls the first in-person panel: Catherine Lucci, Joshua Epstein, Scott Folletta, Rosa Cohen-Cruz, and Isabel Ortega Romero. She instructs them to begin when seated.
chapters.title: Chair calls first public panel

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Catherine Lucci from AV Anti-Violence Project.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Joshua Epstein from the Brooklyn Defender Services.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Scott Folletta from Neighborhood Defender Services of Harlem.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Rosa Cohen-Cruz from the Bronx Defenders.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And Isabel Ortega Romero from the Brooklyn Borough President's Office.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Josh Epstein, immigration practice director at Brooklyn Defender Services, says the office serves over 40,000 people annually. He supports the Cut Ties with ICE package and explains how DOC transfers clients to ICE without due process, urging passage of Intros 1077-A and 1078-A.
chapters.title: Josh Epstein of Brooklyn Defender Services supports bills

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: My name is Josh Epstein, and I'm the director of the immigration practice at Brooklyn Defender Services Queens office.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you to the committee and Sharon Cunacion for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Brooklyn Defenders is a public defense office providing criminal, family, and immigration defense to over 40,000 people annually in Brooklyn and Queens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Every day we witness how criminal court contacts expose immigrant New Yorkers to unequal treatment that can lead to double punishment, even after New York City criminal cases are resolved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: BDS strongly supports the CUT ties with ICE legislative package, which would close dangerous gaps in the law that allow the NYPD and DOC to funnel New Yorkers into the deportation machine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: DOC assists with the transfer of our clients to ICE custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Our clients aren't afforded due process as DOC transmits information about our clients to ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: This can happen after a client resolved a prior case for certain convictions and is rearrested

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: even if that new case is still pending.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: These clients cannot defend themselves in their New York City case while they are incarcerated in dangerous and deadly immigration detention centers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Intro 1078A would resolve this problem because the DOC would not be able to communicate with ICE unless a federal judge has signed a warrant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Judicial review is critical to protect New Yorkers'rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Immigration detainers are signed by Homeland Security officers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: They are not reviewed by a judge.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: An intro 1077A would ensure that the NYPD cannot engage in the detention of New Yorkers without a warrant signed by a judge.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Our community members are at risk of being lost to a detention and deportation system with egregious human rights abuses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Intro 1077A ensures judicial review before the NYPD helps ICE in detaining New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

chapters.summary: Catherine Luch, attorney at the New York City Anti-Violence Project, says LGBTQ and HIV-affected immigrants live in fear of ICE. She describes a transgender client in an all-male detention center and supports the Cut Ties with ICE legislative package.
chapters.title: Catherine Luch of Anti-Violence Project supports cut ties package

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: First, we would like to thank everyone at this public hearing, especially those who are at the forefront of the efforts to defend and support our immigrant neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: To the Committee on Immigration, thank you for holding this public hearing to examine the current state of immigration enforcement activity in New York City,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: and in particular for hearing two critical bills, the ICE out of NYPD and the ICE out of Department of Corrections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: I am Catherine Luch, an attorney at the New York City Anti-Violence Project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: AVP serves New York City's LGBTQ and HIV-affected communities, many of whom are immigrants who live in constant fear of ICE detentions or deportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: They do not feel safe because of the increasingly lethal violence with which ICE executes its mission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: One of our clients, a transgender woman who came to New York City seeking safety from the transphobic violence in her home country,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: is currently sitting in an all-male immigration detention center in Louisiana.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: In detention, she has experienced transphobic attacks and violent harassment from guards and has been denied access to necessary medical care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: She

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: is in solitary confinement because the detention facility determined she would not be safe with the general all-male population.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: She's not only cut off from her community, but she's also cut off from the sun and the outside world entirely because she is a trans woman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: This is the treatment that our queer and trans immigrants are subjected to, and this is why they currently live in fear and do not feel safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: AVP expresses its support for the CUT ties with ICE legislative package, which includes the ICE out of NYPD, the ICE out of DOC, and the New York City Sanctuary Trust Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: We join ICE Out NYC Coalition in its call on the City Council to pass these bills immediately.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: No one is safe until all, including LGBTQ immigrant New Yorkers, are safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: These critical bills aim to protect our communities from ICE and to strengthen accountability measures when our agencies fail to do exactly that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: They must be passed without delay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Luch
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to lend our voice in support of the Cut Ties with ICE legislative package.

chapters.summary: Scott Folletta of Neighborhood Defender Service of Harlem describes a 2022 client handed to ICE at Manhattan Criminal Courthouse in violation of detainer law. He says the client spent 18 months in detention and calls for the Cut Ties package and accountability.
chapters.title: Scott Folletta of Neighborhood Defender Service describes client case

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: Scott Folletta for the Neighborhood Defender Service of Harlem, a holistic public community-based public defender office that serves the Upper Manhattan community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: Thank you for holding this hearing and for hearing us out today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: I want to talk a little bit about what it looks like when local law enforcement

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: cooperates with ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: In 2022, a client of NDS was handed by local officers to ICE at the Manhattan Criminal Courthouse, just down the street here, in violation of New York City's detainer law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: Without knowing what was happening, he was hustled into a van, driven across state lines, and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: to what he later would learn is an immigration jail, when other detainees told him, we are going to be deported.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: He felt like he had just been kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: Within days, he started suffering from medical conditions that ICE did not treat, resulting in excessive bleeding, the loss of 50 pounds of weight before he was finally hospitalized.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: And he was terrified of the possibility of being deported to Ukraine, a war-torn country from which he had fled as a child from ethnic violence, in which he had been doused with gasoline and almost set on fire.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: After filing applications, motions, appeals, bond requests, habeas litigation, our attorneys were finally able to free our client, but only after he had spent a year and a half in ICE detention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: Our client succeeded.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: experience is not unique.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: When advocates discovered through FOIL requests that DOC had actively and knowingly cooperated with ICE in violating our sanctuary laws during the last Trump administration, the agencies before this committee

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: basically responded with a shrug saying that was in the past, won't happen again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: And did not identify a single incident of discipline that occurred as a result of those violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: NYPD testified today that they had not cooperated with a ICE detainer in the last 10 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: It was an NYPD sergeant who called ICE in our client's case and invited them to come to the courthouse to pick him up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: No discipline was identified in that case for our client.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: It's a transparency and accountability black hole, which is why we join our colleagues here to call for the cut ties package to be passed and to draw a clear line.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: We will not be complicit in any of ICE's attacks on our communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Scott Folletta
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Rosa Cohen-Cruz, Director of Immigration Policy at Bronx Defenders, supports all legislation and focuses on Intro 1078. She says DOC continues to transfer people to ICE without judicial warrants and calls for the NYC Sanctuary Trust Act for accountability.
chapters.title: Rosa Cohen-Cruz of Bronx Defenders supports 1078 and accountability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Good morning or good afternoon now, Chair and committee members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: My name is Rosa Cohen-Cruz.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: I'm the Director of Immigration Policy for the Bronx Defenders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: The Bronx Defenders is supportive of all the legislation on today's agenda, and we specifically want to focus on the entire full cut.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Cut ties legislative package.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Intro 1077, I was pleased to hear the NYPD supports that bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: It simply brings the law up to date, as you heard, and so I'm going to focus my time on 1078, which is a long

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: overdue bill that would ensure the Department of Corrections can no longer violate the spirit of the detainer laws by clearly prohibiting the transfer of custody without a judicial warrant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: It is notable that the Department of Corrections isn't here today, despite the fact that they've been caught multiple times violating the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: I will say again that they were caught sending emails using the hashtag team send them back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: So we're at times that may have been inadvertent, other times it was done with overt anti-immigrant animus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: At the March 6, 2026 hearing before the oversight committee in this council, James Conroy confirmed that DOC continues to transfer custody of individuals despite not ever have being presented with a judicial warrant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: The department claimed that if a person has a qualifying conviction, a judicial warrant isn't necessary as long as they don't hold a person beyond their release time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: This disregards the statutes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: plain language and it clearly undermines the due process protections the council had deliberately enacted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: The department has reported that in fiscal year 26, they've transferred 24 people using New York City's resources into ICE custody, which is a deadly agency as we've been talking about today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: So we strongly support interest 1078.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: To clear up any confusion to the extent it even exists about the requirement of law to ensure a judicial warrant is prevented before DOC can communicate or transfer custody to ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Finally, in order to really enact these bills correctly, we need full accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: And Inter 739 does add a new layer of training and implementation, but we also need to ensure that we have the full accountability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: within the New York City Sanctuary Trust Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Without this bill, we will, the slap on the wrist that the NYPD described in their testimony is simply not enough to ensure accountability with these laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: The final thing I'll say is please do not make us come back here to testify about these laws again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: We have been here for five years telling the same stories.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: My clients, many of them who came before this council and told their stories are shared through us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Some of them have been deported.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: They have been harmed immensely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: We have made a record time and time again about how harmful this collusion has been, and it is time for this council to take action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Isabel Ortega Romero represents the Brooklyn Borough President and supports Intros 1077, 1078, and 739, plus Resolution 729. She describes the Marble Hill shooting and calls for mandatory disciplinary action and fines for repeat sanctuary violations.
chapters.title: Isabel Ortega Romero of Brooklyn BP supports bills and accountability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Hi, I'm back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: I hope you're not sick of me yet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Good afternoon and thank you, Chair Encarnacion, for holding this hearing today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: My name is Isabel Ortega Romero, and I'm here representing the office of the Brooklyn Borough President.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: The last time I appeared before you on behalf of the Borough President, I testified about the importance of codifying the recommendation from Mayor Mamdani's Executive Order 13 and limiting law enforcement's cooperation with ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: We are relieved to see the City Council spearheading the fight to protect vulnerable New Yorkers and to ensure that our taxpayer dollars are used to assist them rather than being complicit in Trump's cruel mass deportation agenda.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Since that hearing, there was a tragedy in Marble Hill on October 8th, where ICE agents shot Oscar Belgal in the neck while his five-year-old son was in the backseat of his car.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: While this did not happen in Brooklyn, Borough President Reynoso is concerned that it reflects a pattern of what happens when federal immigration agents are made to feel they can operate freely in our city without facing any accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Mayor Mamdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch both stated explicitly that the NYPD had no advance notice of the federal operation that no officers were present when the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Shots were fired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: However, there was public perception, which is something I heard that was brought up multiple times, that the NYPD had assisted ICE by clearing the way for federal agents to take Oscar into custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: The NYPD also escalated tensions and protests against ISIS brutality by deploying officers to arrest and push back demonstrators outside of New York Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where Oscar was being treated for his wounds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: We must make sure there are no blurred lines between the New York City agencies and federal immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: This is why Borough President Reynoso supports Intros 1077 and 1078.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: I'm not going to describe the laws because I'm running out of time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: A detainer request from ICE is not a judicial warrant and publicly funded NYPD and DOC resources should not be used to hold New Yorkers so that federal immigration agents can circumvent the legal system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: The borough president further supports Intro 0739.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: This bill would ensure that if a city worker is approached by ICE or any other outside law enforcement agency with a request related to immigration enforcement, they must decline unless they have consulted with and received a sign-off from agency leadership or the legal department.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: This way, no city worker can take it upon themselves to circumvent or sanctuary city laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: I am going to go over a little bit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Lastly, we strongly support Resolution 0729.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Our office has received multiple requests from constituents'families seeking pro bono deportation defense for their loved ones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Although many legal service providers are already doing incredible work, and we commend them for that work, the need far outweighs their capacity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: And too often, we have had to tell these families that there's no one available to take their case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: No family should hear that when a loved one is facing deportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: And this is why I'm going a little bit over.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: We do support this legislation, but one of the borough president's recommendations still stands.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: The city council should establish mandatory disciplinary action, fines, the removal of officers, employees, and agency leadership, and other enforcement mechanisms for repeat violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Training and codifying guidance are merely the beginning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Once a city employee has been trained, given clear directives, and is bound by the law, any cooperation with ICE is no longer a misunderstanding of the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: It is a choice, and it should carry consequences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Far too many families have been torn apart and brutalized, and far too many warrantless arrests have taken place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: We hope the City Council will take the next step and ensure that agencies and employees are held accountable and responsible for knowingly breaking the law, as our immigrant neighbors deserve to feel safe in their own city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Thank you again for holding this hearing today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: We look forward to continue to work alongside you in ensuring that city government advances justice, honors the legal protections meant to prevent unlawful persecution of New Yorkers who call the city home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Thank you again.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: That was more than a little bit, but I'll allow it.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: No, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I'm going to call up the next panel, Spencer Reynolds from the Legal Defense Fund, Nick Klein from New York County.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Defender Services.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Hina Navid from La Colmena.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Ladies de la Rosa, also from La Comena.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And Jacqueline.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Gold Swag Pants?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Penance.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Oh, you teach me.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Legal Aid Society.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you all, and you may begin.

chapters.summary: Spencer Reynolds, attorney with the NAACP Legal Defense Fund, says gaps in sanctuary protections harm Black and brown immigrants, protesters, and legal observers. He asks the council to pass the Curb Act, end data transfers to ICE, and pass the NYC Trust Act.
chapters.title: Spencer Reynolds of NAACP LDF calls for closing gaps

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Encarnacion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: My name is Spencer Reynolds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: I'm an attorney with the NAACP Legal Defense Fund and a former U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: Department of Homeland Security domestic intelligence lawyer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: While New York has taken steps to limit cooperation with ICE, significant gaps remain and harm black and brown immigrants, protesters,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: legal observers, and people impacted by the NYPD's discriminatory gang policing practices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: The City Council must close these gaps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: After ICE shot New Yorker Oscar Belgal on October 8th, the NYPD escalated the situation by providing security for ICE agents and their vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: In 2025, when ICE targeted West African vendors on Canal Street, the NYPD provided crowd management support, arresting several protesters who were later released without charges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: The NYPD puts information into data systems directly operated by DHS and hosts DHS intelligence officers who acquire local data to assist ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: and other federal law enforcement activities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: Last year, the NYPD joined the FBI in an intelligence report calling peaceful immigration court watchers terrorists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: And the NYPD openly participates in President Trump's Homeland Security Task Forces, which conduct gang and drug policing, NYPD practices that rely on its racially discriminatory, inaccurate gang database.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: Current New York law does not prohibit this collaboration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: Fortunately, there are steps that the council can and should take today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: First, we ask that you pass the Curb Act to direct the NYPD not interfere with peaceful anti-ICE protest through the deployment of specialized units or dangerous tactics.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: Second, mandate that city agencies cease data transfers to ICE and other federal law enforcement, including through unregulated indirect means.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: Necessary sharing with the federal government should be done in limited, transparent ways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: Finally, pass the NYC Trust Act to make protections enforceable by members of the public who are harmed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: The Council has the power to end New York City's involvement in ICE's harmful, violent operations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Spencer Reynolds
utterances.text: We urgently ask that you exercise that power.

chapters.summary: Nick Klein, immigration attorney at New York County Defender Services, focuses on the ICE Out of DOC Act. He says DOC fails to provide basic information about clients and cannot be trusted to comply with detainer law, urging passage of the Cut Ties package.
chapters.title: Nick Klein of NY County Defender Services on DOC failures

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: Council members, thank you for the time today and for holding this meeting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: My name is Nick Klein.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: I'm one of the immigration attorneys at New York County Defender Services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: This testimony will focus primarily on the ICE out of DOC Act, but NYCDA strongly stands behind everything that's being discussed today, all the bills.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: Our office experiences firsthand how gaps in the sanctuary protections put our clients at risk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: The existing loopholes in the administrative code leave enormous room for agency employees to misunderstand or intentionally circumvent the detainer law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: At this point, the record is clear that DOC cannot be trusted to comply with this law, and it is therefore long past time that the Council act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: When we inquire about the release of specific clients, DOC routinely fails to provide even basic information regarding whether they will be released from DOC custody back into our community or whether they will be handed over to ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: Often DOC does not respond to our communications at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: So it is particularly offensive when we hear that they have been willfully communicating with ICE about our clients and coordinating the transfer to immigration custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: This is what happened to a client of ours during the Adams administration last year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: Even when the sanctuary protections and the detainer laws clearly apply, obtaining confirmation from DOC can be impossible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: My colleagues and I have spent untold hours trying to get in touch with DOC to remind them of their legal obligations and to ensure that they follow them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: For us, this is a logistical hurdle and a waste of precious time and resources, but for clients and their families, it is a terrifying experience riddled with uncertainty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: Not taking action now to resolve the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: uncertainties in these laws will result in more members of our community being funneled into the already deadly immigration system, a system that has time and time again revealed itself as cruel, arbitrary, and lacking in basic due process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: It should be clear to all of us now that the consequences of our failure to act thus far are not merely procedural or theoretical.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: They can be irreversible, costing New Yorkers their ability to remain in their homes and communities where, under our detainer laws, they're supposed to already be protected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: We need clear and forcible rules that eliminate these loopholes and ensure meaningful accountability, and we therefore urge the Council to finally pass the Cut Ties with ICE package.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nick Klein
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Hina Naveed, executive director of La Colmena and a DACA recipient, describes ICE arresting a father in front of his children on Staten Island. She supports the legislation and urges funding for rapid response and legal services.
chapters.title: Hina Naveed of La Colmena describes ICE fear and supports bills

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chia Encarnacion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: My name is Hina Naveed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: I'm the executive director of La Colmena on Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: La Colmena has been on the front lines of responding to ICE arrests and detentions, coordinating legal assistance, and supporting families facing deportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: I am an immigration attorney.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: I'm also an undocumented immigrant with DACA protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: As ICE brutality is intensifying in our neighborhoods, I'm here not only as an advocate, but also as a wife, a mother, and part of the community being targeted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: Just this morning, according to the account shared with me, ICE descended as a father prepared his children for school in Port Richmond on Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: Their vehicle struck a neighbor's car.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: Six to eight officers dragged him away, bleeding in front of his crying child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: That fear reaches into my home too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: My husband also has DACA and provides immigration legal services in Port Richmond.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: When I hear ICE has taken someone, I always wonder, is it him?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: When am I going to tell my daughter?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: We've planned already who would care for our daughter if we were detained.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: As an attorney, I also sit with families already living that separation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: During a Zoom consultation with the detained father, I had helped his family join so they could have some time together.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: His young daughter asked when he was coming home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: Trying to protect her, he told her he was at work and would be back as soon as he could.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: No legal consultation can give that child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: which she was actually asking for, her father to come home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: This is why La Colmena has long called for ICE's abolition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: As community members have said, and as Commissioner Ali highlighted today, ICE is lawless and a rogue agency that cannot be reformed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: In the meantime, New York City has to do all that we can do to ensure we're not helping ICE tear families apart and terrorize our communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: As your report cites, city personnel sharing information in violation of sanctuary laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: This is very serious.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: It erodes trust.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: Leaves neighbors afraid to seek help, or even attend today's hearing or the rally that's coming up because they feared ISIS presence or cooperation with NYPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: That fear is following people into decisions about whether to attend a meeting, seek help, or speak out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: People with every reason to speak are afraid to be heard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: I'm just going to take a few more seconds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: I know my time is almost up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: We at La Colmena support the legislation and the resolution before you, and we urge you to close the loopholes, require training, and enforce sanctuary protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: Please back those protections with funding for Staten Island's community-based rapid response as well as sustained legal services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: Families need both immediate support and ongoing representation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: Turning to our city should bring protection, not put us at risk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hina Naveed
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Lady Zela Rosa, advocacy coordinator at La Colmena, says fear of immigration enforcement prevents workers from reporting abuse and seeking services. She supports Intros 739, 1077, and 1078 and urges multilingual explanations and accessible reporting.
chapters.title: Lady Zela Rosa of La Colmena on workers' rights and sanctuary

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Encarnacion, members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: My name is Lady Zela Rosa, and I'm the advocacy coordinator at La Colmena.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: We work with day laborers, domestic workers, and other low-wage immigrant workers on Staten Island through organizing education, culture, and equitable economic development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: And I want to focus today on what sanctuary protections mean for workers'ability to stand up for their rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: At La Colmena, we see how the fear of immigration enforcement affects whether workers feel safe reporting abuse, seeking assistance, accessing city services, or really going out of their house.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: When a worker is deciding whether to report unpaid wages or an unsafe workplace, immigration consequences should not be part of that calculation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: The decision should be about how to enforce their rights, not whether asking for help could put themselves or their family at risk.
