utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: And that's why we support the legislation before you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: Intro 739 addresses an essential question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: Do the city employees who interact with their communities know what sanctuary laws require and what to do when immigration authorities request information or assistance?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: Training and public implementation protocols must give employees clear instructions, not leave workers'safety dependent on who happens to answer a question or to handle a request.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: We also support Intro 1077 and 1078 to strengthen restrictions on detention and cooperation with federal immigration authorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: local government should not become a pathway into immigration custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: So as the council advances these bills, we urge you to make implementation accessible to the workers these protections are meant to reach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: Publish clear, multilingual explanation of the rules.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: Make it easy to report suspected violations and understand what happens after a report.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: Work with community organizations to ensure that workers know their rights and can identify when those rights have been violated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: Immigrant workers are organizing, supporting one another, and demanding fair treatment, and the city's responsibility is to ensure that they can exercise their rights without immigration enforcement being used to silence them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lady Zela Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz, legal fellow at the Legal Aid Society, describes a client called Byron who received a youthful offender adjudication but was turned over to ICE a day before release. She supports ICE Out of DOC and the NYC Trust Act for accountability.
chapters.title: Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz of Legal Aid describes Byron case

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: My name is Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz, and I'm a legal fellow with the Legal Aid Society.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: I'm testifying today on behalf of the Legal Aid Society's immigration practice and our criminal defense practice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: Our clients face and their attorneys witness firsthand the consequences of when the Department of Corrections and the NYPD

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: collaborate with federal immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: As has been shared today, the Executive Order 13 audit found that DOC responded to 24 ICE detainer requests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: And I want to tell the committee about a legal aid client who we'll call Byron.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: Byron was a young man seeking asylum.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: He was arrested after a fight between him and some other young people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: Byron's defense attorney negotiated an immigration safe plea that would leave him with a youthful offender adjudication.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: The detainer law specifically exempts YO adjudications from the definition of a violent or serious crime, and YO adjudications are not considered convictions for immigration law purposes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: But a detainer was lodged for Byron.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: And when his defense attorney reached out to DOC for assurances that Byron would be released to his family and not to ICE, as the law requires, DOC was non-responsive, as Nick shared.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: We spent many, many hours working for clarity from DOC, and we didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: Rather than follow the law, GOC turned Byron over to ICE a day before he was meant to be released.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: Legal aid has raised this violation with the Council before, but it remains an important touchstone for why we need

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: both ICE out of DOC and also the NYC Trust Act, because there needs to be accountability when there are violations of our sanctuary laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: To the important bills that are on the committee's agenda today, the Legal Aid Society thanks the council for their support, thanks the agencies that were here earlier today for their support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: We strongly support ISAT of NYPD and ISAT of DOC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: No New Yorker's information should be shared with ICE absent a judicial warrant, full stop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: And no New Yorker should face prolonged detention by the NYPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: But the city's laws need to be compliant with extra wells.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Goldsack-Pantz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And I call up Rachel Goldberg.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Tinu Kim.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Razim Zaman and Stephanie Kweng.

chapters.summary: Stephanie Kwong, Deputy Director of Social Services at Homecrest Community Services, describes serving immigrant families in southern Brooklyn. She supports Resolution 729 and the BUILD Act to strengthen immigration legal service capacity.
chapters.title: Stephanie Kwong of Homecrest Community Services supports Reso 729

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Encarnacion and members of the Committee on Immigration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: My name is Stephanie Kwong, Deputy Director of Social Services at Homecrest Community Services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: For nearly 30 years, Homecrest has provided essential services to immigrant families, older adults, and underserved communities in southern Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: We are testifying today alongside the Asian American Federation, which coordinates the Rapid Immigration Support and Empowerment RISE Network.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: Homecrest is a member of this network of nearly 20 Asian-led and Asian-serving organizations providing immigration case management and legal services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: Services to support New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: At Homecrest, our staff assist immigrant clients with green card renewals, naturalization applications, supporting documents, and referrals to trusted legal service providers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: We also provide multilingual outreach and Know Your Rights information to help community members understand their rights and navigate changing immigration policies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: For many of the residents we serve, particularly older adults with limited English proficiency, understanding government procedures and accessing services already present significant challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: Ongoing immigration enforcement has created confusion and uncertainty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: Some residents may not understand the difference between

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: between local government agencies and federal immigration authorities, or may worry about how their personal information could be used.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: These concerns can discourage people from seeking government assistance and accessing essential services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: Resolution 729-2026, which calls for passage

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: of the Building Up Immigrant Legal Defense Build Act, addresses the need to strengthen immigration legal service capacity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: Community-based organizations like HomeCrest help residents navigate complicated systems and connect with trusted legal assistance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: But effective referrals depend on living

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: on having enough qualified legal service providers to meet community needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: We ask the city to continue work closely with trusted community-based organizations to provide accurate, up-to-date, multilingual information and strengthen the support for immigration case management, legal referrals, and community education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephanie Kwong
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

chapters.summary: Taehyun Kim, program manager at the Asian American Federation, says ICE arrests of Asian immigrants increased 436% nationwide and New York ranks third. He supports Intros 1077, 1078, and 739 and calls for language access and partnerships with Asian-led organizations.
chapters.title: Taehyun Kim of Asian American Federation on Asian immigrant arrests

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair and members of the Committee on Immigration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: My name is Taehyun Kim, and I serve as a program manager at the Asian American Federation, where we work to uplift the collective voice of Asian New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: AF also convenes the Rapid Immigration Support and Empowerment RISE Network, a coalition of Asian-led and Asian-serving CBOs dedicated to supporting and protecting immigrant communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: Asian immigrants are too often overlooked in conversations about immigration enforcement, despite experiencing a disproportionate increase in federal enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: According to Stop AAPI Hate, as reported by Documented, nationwide ICE arrests of Asian immigrants have increased by 436% under the current administration, nearly double the increase among immigrants overall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: New York ranks third nationwide in ICE arrests of Asian immigrants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: Average monthly arrests statewide have more than quadrupled from 24 to 103.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: Between January 2025 and August 2026, ICE arrested nearly 1,600 immigrants from South and East Asian countries in New York alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: The consequences extend beyond those directly targeted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: In our forthcoming study of over 120 Asian and Latino-owned businesses in Jackson Heights and Sunset Park, approximately half independently identified immigration enforcement as a

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: a factor affecting their businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: When immigrants fear moving freely throughout our city, entire communities and local economies suffer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: New York City's sanctuary laws are fundamental to its identity as a city of immigrants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: Yet existing loopholes and inconsistent implementation undermine these protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: AF strongly urges the council to pass Intro 1077 and 1078 to close loopholes in the NYPD and DOC detainer laws and Intro 739 to strengthen agency training, transparency, and accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: Equally important, the city must ensure meaningful language access, equitable investments in immigration legal services, and formal partnerships with trusted Asian-led and Asian-serving organizations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: AF and our RISE network partners look forward to working alongside the council and the administration to build a more inclusive, equitable, and coordinated response that meaningfully addresses the needs of Asian immigrant communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Taehyun Kim
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today and for your continued commitment to protecting New York City's immigrant communities.

chapters.summary: Razin Zaman of the Asian American Legal Defense and Education Fund describes Southeast Asian refugees facing deportation for decades-old convictions. He supports Intros 1077-A, 1078-A, and 739 and says sharing release dates tells ICE when to wait at Rikers.
chapters.title: Razin Zaman of AALDEF on Southeast Asian deportations

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Encarnacion and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: My name is Razin Zaman and I'm here from the Asian American Legal Defense and Education Fund.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: We strongly urge the Council to pass Intros 1077A, 1078A, and 739.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: We represent many Southeast Asian refugees who fled the Vietnam War, known as the American War to many in the community, and genocide as children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: They were accepted into this country as refugees and resettled in neighborhoods with underfunded schools and heavy policing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: For some, being pushed out of school began a path that led to arrest, incarceration, and a deportation order.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: Today, decades after they served their time, the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: Government still tries to deport them based on these decades-old convictions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: The fact that a conviction occurred decades ago offers no protection against deportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: Nearly four in five Southeast Asians deported in 2025 and 2026 had convictions at least a decade old.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: More than half had convictions at least 20 years old.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: Our clients, mostly in their 50s and 60s, still see the consequences of the expanded school-to-prison-to-deportation pipeline today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: People arrested as teenagers who served their sentences decades ago are now parents fighting to stay with their children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: One father we represent has been a New Yorker for nearly half a century.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: He arrived at the age of seven as a stateless refugee after the Khmer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: Rouge killed his father and sister.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: He was 18 and a student at Bronx Community College when he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: He spent two and a half years on Rikers awaiting trial.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: An immigration judge ordered him deported while he was incarcerated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: Immigration officers were waiting for him when he was released.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: He spent nearly two more years in immigration detention because no country would accept him as a deportee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: When our client was finally released from immigration detention, he had nowhere to live.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: For more than 20 years now, he has overseen repairs and renovations at a 200-bed housing facility for men in New York experiencing homelessness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: In August, ICE told him it intends to detain him again and deport him to Cambodia, which has never recognized him as a citizen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: If Cambodia refuses to accept him, ICE can send him to a third country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: Human Rights Watch has documented that the United States has sent individuals from Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam to Eswatini, where they were held in maximum security prisons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: Even just sharing an individual's release date tells ICE when to be waiting at Rikers Gate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: The city's own audit found that in 2025, jail staff notified ICE of releases and helped transfer people into custody in 24 cases under exceptions in city law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: 1077A and 1078A would end those exceptions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: We urge you to pass these bills and end New York City's partnership with ICE in imposing cruel double punishment and irreversible family suffering.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Razin Zaman
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you for sharing.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I'm now going to call up to the dais Pantia Nori, Paul Padilla Lopez, Rachel Jordan, sorry, I thought it was Y, Abina Hutchful.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Pantea Nori, paralegal at DOORS Legal Services Center, says young immigrant clients are dropping out of school and afraid to attend hearings and ICE check-ins. She supports the Cut Ties with ICE legislation package.
chapters.title: Pantea Nori of DOORS Legal Services on youth fear

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: Good afternoon, my name is Pantea Nori and I am a paralegal with the DOORS Legal Services Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: The DOOR is a comprehensive youth development organization serving up to 11,000 young people annually across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: All of the young people I work with apply for special immigrant juvenile status in addition to asylum.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: These young clients are required to attend their court hearings, biometrics appointments, ICE check-ins, all while learning English, attending school, working multiple jobs, and planning for their future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: The presence of ICE in New York City has directly hindered my clients'efforts to become productive members of society.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: For example, several of my clients, all with promising futures, have decided to drop out of school due to fear of ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: At our weekly clinic for pro se young immigrants, many young people are scared to attend their hearings and ICE check-ins.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: all of which are necessary to obtain legal status.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: Many young people request to attend their hearings virtually, despite immigration judges denying most motions to appear remotely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: Even with the recent decision on the courthouse arrest case, the fear of ISAT courts remains present.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: Another client of mine chose not to attend her sister's wedding due to fear of ICE arrests at airports.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: How can young immigrants be expected to follow the requirements of their legal case and become a part of society while ICE is allowed to freely roam our schools, courtrooms, and airports?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: The pressure on immigrant communities and families is immense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: Young immigrants, their relatives, and friends are forced into an impossible situation where pursuing legal status entails the risk of becoming dangerously visible to immigration authorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: This is why we ask New York City to stand with immigrant New Yorkers and cut ties with ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: More specifically, we strongly need your support in the passage of the Cut Tides with ICE legislation package.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Pantea Nori
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

chapters.summary: Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez of DOORS Legal Services Center describes a 21-year-old client detained by ICE and now afraid of any law enforcement encounter. He urges passage of the bills and the Curb Act to end NYPD and DOC cooperation with ICE.
chapters.title: Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez of DOORS on young immigrant detention

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Encarnacion and the committee members on immigration.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: We broke it.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Go for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: My name is Paul Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez, and I'm a legal administrative assistant at the Doors Legal Services Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: The Doors is a comprehensive youth development organization, as my colleague has said previously, reaching 11,000 teens and young adults each year for the past 54 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: But behind these figures sit young immigrant New Yorkers, profoundly constrained,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: by fear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: This past summer, a dorm member, a 21-year-old young person with a pending humanitarian visa, has seen his world shrink to two places, his home at a Brooklyn shelter and a safe place at the door.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: Although released on a habeas petition following nearly two months of harrowing ICE detention,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: He now fears and cries encounters with any law enforcement agency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: So much so that at one point his fear rendered him seriously hospitalized one day before his immigration court hearing, to which he nevertheless bravely attended the next day, but was detained unlawfully at court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: He fears and cries that an ordinary encounter with the NYPD could expose his whereabouts to immigration authorities and place him at risk of warrantless detention once again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: But his story is not alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: It echoes across the lives of thousands of young immigrant New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: In September and December of 2025, New York City's own Department of Investigation documented a DOC investigator providing ICE with real-time release information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: And an NYPD officer using sometimes outdated and erroneous police databases and terrorist screenings to flag encounters with individuals targeted for immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: Such findings expose the divide between the protections that are lost promise and the violations that our agencies fail to prevent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: This council can narrow that divide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: This council can end the NYPD's remaining detainer exceptions and restrict its assistance with immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: This council can prohibit DOC from sharing custodial information with immigration authorities or facilitating civil immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: This council can also pass the Curb Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: And this council can finally imbue young New Yorkers, especially black and brown New Yorkers, disproportionately harmed by the unlawful detention and prohibited cooperation, an open door to seek justice in court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: We urge you to pass these bills and make that promise real for every young New Yorker who finds their voice at the door today and who may one day find that voice raised in these very chambers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Paul Anthony Padilla Lopez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Rachel Jordan, managing attorney at Safe Passage Project, describes an unaccompanied minor from Guinea placed by ACS on Long Island and arrested by ICE. She urges the committee to ensure immigrant children in ACS custody are placed within New York City.
chapters.title: Rachel Jordan of Safe Passage Project on ACS placement outside NYC

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: My deep thanks to Chair Encarnacion and the committee for holding this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: My name is Rachel Jordan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: I'm the Managing Attorney for Advocacy at Safe Passage Project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: We provide free legal services to over 1,600 immigrant children and youth living in New York City and Long Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: I believe strongly that the bills under discussion today will better protect New York City residents from ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: But the most vulnerable New Yorkers of all,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: who are unaccompanied children in the custody of the New York Administration for Children's Services, continue to fall through the cracks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: And this happens when ACS places an immigrant child in a care setting outside of New York City where that child has no protections at all under the city's sanctuary laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: Our organization represents one such child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: I will call him Omar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: Omar is an unaccompanied minor from Guinea.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: At 16, he was placed in ACS custody after his brother beat him and kicked him out of his home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: Manhattan Family Court found him to be a destitute child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: Omar came to safe passage after he'd been ordered deported for missing an immigration court hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: As we moved to reopen his immigration proceedings, ACS moved him from a Manhattan placement to a group home on Long Island, where he told us repeatedly that he felt unsafe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: We also learned he had a pending criminal case in Suffolk County.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: He was clearly a sitting duck for ICE enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: We warned ACS about this repeatedly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: We asked them to move him back to Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: That never happened.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: Suffolk police took Omar from his group home to a police station where ICE was waiting outside to arrest him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: They claimed he was an adult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: Despite overwhelming evidence, he was a 16-year-old child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: He was in ICE custody for over three months.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: He suffered serious mental and physical harm, including being attacked by adult detainees and being placed in solitary confinement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: He's still in federal custody, though now in a juvenile facility after we provided a new birth certificate from Guinea.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: We have received no assurances from ACS that if released from federal custody, ACS will be able to place Omar within New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: None of this needed to happen had ACS placed Omar within New York City instead of out on Long Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: I do believe that the city's sanctuary measures would have stopped him from being turned over to immigration officials.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: And I urge the members of this committee to work with the city agencies to ensure that immigrant kids in ACS custody are placed within the confines of New York City to ensure their protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Jordan
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: It's given me a lot to think about.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Calling up next, Whitney Bronstein, sorry, Zachary Ahmad.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Elcio?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Is that like my name?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Love that.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Flores.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And that's a B.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: V&A Romero.

chapters.summary: Whitney Bronstein, senior attorney at the Immigrant Defense Project, says NYPD and DOC routinely violate due process and exploit exceptions in sanctuary laws. She supports Intros 1077-A and 1078-A and calls for ending ICE collusion in all forms.
chapters.title: Whitney Bronstein of Immigrant Defense Project supports bills

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: My name is Whitney Bronstein and I am a senior attorney for community defense at the Immigrant Defense Project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: IDP was founded nearly 30 years ago to combat the targeting of immigrants for nasty deportation to fight for justice for all immigrants, in particular those targeted by the racist criminal and immigration legal systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: IDP is here in support of introductions 1077A and 1078A, as well as intro 209, which we know is not on the hearing list for today, but it is part of our cut ties with ICE legislative package.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Through fear-mongering under the guise of public safety, NYPD and DOC violate New Yorkers'due process rights as a matter of course.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: For immigrant New Yorkers, our 2014 laws restricting these agencies from colluding with ICE were critical pieces of legislation that we advocated for and stand by.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Yet, in the years since, we have documented routine violations as well as exploitation of the exceptions in our laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: In particular, in hearings going back to 2021, we have sounded the alarm bell on routine illegal communication.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: between DOC and ICE that we demonstrated through foil production of email correspondence, including frequent delays and slowdowns of people's release to facilitate their arrest by ICE, and an email signed hashtag team send them back as part of ample evidence of regular unrecorded communication.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Since then, it has become clearer than ever that ICE has no place in our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Our city council holds a deep responsibility in this moment to act robustly and comprehensively to ensure that our city's commitment to welcoming and protecting immigrants is ironclad.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Our city agencies should protect New Yorkers, not facilitate federal immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: IDP runs a hotline to provide advice to immigrant New Yorkers who have had contact with the criminal legal system, as well as their legal advocates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: We get regular calls on our hotline from community members and attorneys alike who are unsure whether an interaction with the NYPD may lead to their information being shared directly with ICE or who have a loved one due to be released from Rikers and returned home and worry that instead they will be funneled to ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: The bills before the committee today will strengthen our city laws, ensuring that they protect every New Yorker equally and demand that ICE provide the necessary documentation when it seeks to compel assistance from city agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Now is the time to end ICE collusion in all of its forms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Zach Ahmad, senior policy counsel at the NYCLU, thanks the Chair for championing Intros 1077-A and 1078-A. He says the bills would eliminate transfers without a judicial warrant and urges passage of Intro 209, the NYC Sanctuary Trust Act.
chapters.title: Zach Ahmad of NYCLU supports 1077A, 1078A, Intro 209

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: My name is Zach Ahmed, and I'm a senior policy counsel at the New York Civil Liberties Union.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: I want to thank Chair Encarnacion for holding this hearing and for being a committed champion of Intro 1077A, the ICE Out of NYPD Act, and Intro 1078A, the ICE Out of DOC Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: Many people in this room have waited a very long time to see this legislation advance, and today's hearing is a really important milestone along that message.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: It's really encouraging to hear you talk about moving this legislation quickly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: You've heard multiple stories today about the terror that ICE has wrought on our city's immigrant communities and how it has destroyed the lives of so many New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: It is beyond clear that ICE is a lawless agency that must be done away with completely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: And while New York City cannot control the fate or the actions of a federal agency, it can make sure that it is doing nothing whatsoever to collude with or otherwise serve ICE's interests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: New York City is in many ways blessed to have some of the longest standing policies in the country that restrict local city employees from colluding with immigration authorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: Yet contrary to city officials, contrary to how city officials sometimes talk about our city sanctuary laws, they do come with an asterisk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: They are implemented in a way that maintains a relationship with ICE and continues funneling people into the deportation machine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: Under the current legal scheme in practice,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: The Department of Correction continues to transfer people directly into ICE custody using a questionable interpretation of city law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: They did this 24 times just last year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: Almost every day, it seems, we hear city officials lambast ICE for its cruelty, while the machinery of city government continues to facilitate these transfers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: It is simply untenable for city officials to decry ICE as a lawless and unaccountable agency and also continuing to work with them to honor detainers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: So Intros 277A and 278, sorry, 1077A and 1078A on today's agenda would eliminate the possibility of transfers without a judicial warrant signed by a judge, full stop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: It would ensure due process for everyone and do away with the harmful good immigrant, bad immigrant model that's built into our city laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: I also, while not on today's agenda, we do also urge the council to pass Intro 209, the NYC Sanctuary Trust Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: This would give teeth to our city laws by allowing people to hold the city accountable in court and provide a disincentive to breaking the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: And we encourage the council to move these bills forward as the cut ties with ICE package.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: I do want to acknowledge that the current mayoral administration, the city is moving in the right direction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: You know, we saw the recent changes to the NYPD's patrol guide that were discussed earlier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: That is a positive signal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: It was encouraging to hear that the NYPD supports Intro 1077A and that the mayor's office supports the spirit of these bills.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: We hope they.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: can get a little farther with that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: But what we need most of all right now is to remove these harmful and confusing carve-outs, and we ask the City Council to move these bills forward as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Ahmad
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Vianney Romero, Director of Programs at Mixteca, describes a mother afraid to attend family court due to misinformation about local agents sharing information with ICE. She supports agency training, clear protocols, and language access.
chapters.title: Vianney Romero of Mixteca on fear and language access

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, Chair Encarnacion and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to share our perspective on the legislation being considered today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: My name is Vianney Romero, and I serve as the Director of Programs at Misteca Organization, a community-based organization serving immigrant communities in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, and throughout New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: At Misteca, we provide immigration legal access, mental health services, health navigation, and other essential resources, regardless of immigration status.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: Through our work, we recognize that immigration enforcement concerns extends beyond legal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: They affect how families interact with public institutions, access services, and make decisions about their safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: Recently, we had a woman, a young mother, that approached Misteca because she was afraid to attend a family court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: This was in relation to an order of protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: She was afraid and had the misinformation that local agents can share information with immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: She expressed that during the time of feeling unsafe, she hesitated to call or contact local enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: out of fear of detention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: This experience illustrates how fear and misinformation can become barriers to seeking protection and obtaining essential services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: Community-based organizations like MISTECA play a critical role in fighting misinformation, building trust, and helping families to understand their rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: For this reason, agency training, clear implementation protocols, and accessible information about city policies are essential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: Language access must also be prioritized, particularly for individuals who speak Spanish and indigenous languages or have limited literacy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: We also encourage the council to consider how immigration enforcement concerns affect mental health, family stability, and survivors of domestic and gender-based violence who may already face significant barriers to seeking protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: As the Council considers these proposals, we encourage continued engagement with community-based organizations and the immigrant New Yorkers directly affected by these policies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vianney Romero
utterances.text: Thank you for your time and for the opportunity to provide testimony.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Kelly Agnew Barajas of Catholic Charities Archdiocese of New York describes increased enforcement fear and high demand for legal services. She supports Intro 739 and the BUILD Act and urges investment in legal services and rapid response.
chapters.title: Kelly Agnew Barajas of Catholic Charities supports Intro 739 and BUILD Act

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: My name is Kelly Agno Barajas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: I represent the Immigrant and Refugee Services Division at Catholic Charities, Archdiocese of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: Every day our programs provide immigration legal services, refugee resettlement support, programs for day laborers, multilingual hotline assistance to immigrant and refugee communities across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: We're seeing firsthand how increased immigration enforcement activity is affecting New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: Beyond the immediate consequences of detention and deportation proceedings, enforcement has created a climate of fear that affects everyday decisions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: Parents hesitate to take children to school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: Workers are avoiding seeking employment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: Families delay medical care and people are reluctant to access public services or report crimes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: The need for legal and community support is significant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: During fiscal year 26, our hotlines received more than 700 calls related to ICE enforcement activity, nearly 650 rapid response calls, and hundreds more related to deportation proceedings in immigration court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: Since September alone, our legal team has come

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: completed dozens of asylum interviews for unaccompanied children, assisted youth pursuing SIG, and managed more than 75 asylum hearings in just two months.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: We're also deeply concerned by enforcement tactics that undermine community trust and public safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: We've received reports of ICE using private parking lots as staging grounds for enforcement actions and witnessed the devastating impact these operations have on immigrant workers and families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: One of our day labor clients has now spent four months in detention after being apprehended at a Home Depot parking lot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: Separated from his community and subjected to repeated transfers among various detention facilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: For these reasons, Catholic Charities strongly supports Intro 739 and the Council's efforts to ensure clear training and guidance for city employees regarding interactions with federal authorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: We also support

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: T-2026-2544 and the BUILD Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: We urge the Council to continue investing in legal services, multilingual public education, rapid response networks, and policies that ensure all New Yorkers can access essential services without fear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Agnew Barajas
utterances.text: Thank you for your leadership and your commitment to New Yorkers'immigrant communities.

chapters.summary: Raquel Batista, interim executive director of Northern Manhattan Coalition for Immigrant Rights, describes her organization's response to the Marble Hill shooting. She supports the legislation and says NYPD's claim that no one was available to coordinate is disingenuous.
chapters.title: Raquel Batista of NMCIR on Marble Hill and supports legislation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: Thank you first for conducting this hearing today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: My name is Raquel Batista.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: I am an attorney and interim executive director of the North

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: Northern Manhattan Coalition for Immigrant Rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: I also served in 2021 as Commissioner of Immigrant Affairs for New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: And I also worked as a supervising attorney at the Asylum Application Health Center during the migrant crisis from 2023 to 2025.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: Northern Manhattan Coalition is a BIA accredited organization serving Northern Manhattan and the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: Our office is located two stops away from Marble Hill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: The ice shooting occurred the day before the reopening of our offices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: Over the last year, Northern Manhattan Coalition Immigrant Rights

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: has faced some internal challenges, and the community has rallied around the organization to assure it continues to serve our immigrant community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: The ICE shooting has made clear the importance of Northern Manhattan Coalition for Immigrant Rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: We have reached out to Marble Hill schools, senior centers, and community leaders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: We have spent time on 225th Street speaking to residents about ISIS presence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: Days after the shooting, ICE continued their presence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: We continue to let Marble Hill residents know we are a few stops away and ready to assist them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: The evening of the protest, I was there and peacefully marched with the community members and leaders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: There were several elected officials.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: For the NYPD to say that there was no one to coordinate, I find a bit disingenuous today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: More needs to be done to properly handle protesters, not to result in protesters being hurt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: NMCIR supports the legislation being put forward today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: NMCIR has been working since 2004 to get ICE out of our jails and to stop coordinating with the criminal justice system in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: Northern Manhattan is also ready to work on responses in our neighborhoods and citywide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: Thank you so much for all of your work, and we continue, and we look forward to continue partnering in protecting our constituent and civil rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raquel Batista
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Karen Justice of the Demilitarized Brooklyn Navy Yard Campaign says the Navy Yard leases space to Cry Precision, which makes tactical gear for ICE. She calls on the committee to ensure the city terminates the lease and upholds sanctuary laws.
chapters.title: Karen Justice on Brooklyn Navy Yard and Cry Precision

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: Do I just push that?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: It's on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: It's on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: My name is Karen Justice, and I'm here on behalf of Demilitarized Brooklyn Navy Yard Campaign, or DBNY,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: a grassroots campaign committed to disrupting the operations of all ICE deportation, genocide, and ecocide profiteers at the Brooklyn Navy Yard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: The Brooklyn Navy Yard is a publicly owned space that was founded on a vision of innovation, sustainability, and inclusive economic development for the people of Brooklyn and New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: Today, that mission is being undermined by the leasing of space to Cry Precision,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: a company that develops, manufactures, and distributes tactical gear to ICE and Border Patrol for the explicit purpose of facilitating federal immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: The Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation, who oversees the Brooklyn Navy Yard for the City of New York, is violating sanctuary laws and Mayor Momdani's Executive Order 13 by leasing city property to Cry Precision.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: The agents who murdered ICU nurse Alex Preddy, the agents deployed to Delaney Hall,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: the agents involved in ICE raids in Los Angeles, Minnesota, and Chicago, as well as here on Canal Street in New York City, were all wearing Cry Precision gear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: The Cry Precision gear used in these executions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: samples was made at the Brooklyn Navy Yard, using city property and taxpayers' money to facilitate federal immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: The Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation is committing further violations by utilizing the NYPD, a publicly funded city resource to protect Cry Precision.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: We call on this committee to ensure that the Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation and the City of New York uphold the city's sanctuary laws and immediately terminate leases to evict Cry Precision.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: Our public resources should go toward community-centered

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: uses like food justice, public housing, youth workforce programs, and climate justice and infrastructure programs, not ICE deportations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: Evict cry precision, evict ICE deportation profiteers, end complicity now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Justice
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Lima Nasrati, immigration attorney at Catholic Charities and member of NYC DSA's Immigrant Justice Working Group, supports the Sanctuary Trust Act and ICE Out of NYPD and DOC Acts. She says knowing rights empowers communities but the burden should not fall on individuals.
chapters.title: Lima Nasrati of Catholic Charities/DSA supports sanctuary bills

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: Good to go?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: You can go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: Hello, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Encarnacion, and to everyone here for the opportunity to speak today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: My name is Lima Nasrati, and I come to you wearing many hats.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: I am the daughter of Afghan asylum seekers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: I am an immigration attorney at Catholic Charities, where I sit in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: And I'm also a member of New York City DSA's Immigrant Justice Working Group.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: I'm here in support of the Sanctuary Trust Act, the ICE Out of NYPD Act, and the ICE Out of DOC Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: The fear and havoc being wreaked by ICE permeates my life both personally and professionally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: As I sit in immigration court waiting rooms, as I try to encourage clients to report crimes committed against them, and as I walk through my own city streets in Queens,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: and in the Bronx for work, hoping that I will not encounter an ICE vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: I feel grateful still to be able to show up in my professional capacity and my advocate capacity to be able to show my immigrant clients and neighbors that they are beloved members of our New York community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: These bills are an opportunity for New York City and the council to do the same, to show up

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: up for its immigrant community members in ways long overdue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: Within New York City's Immigrant Justice Working Group, I help lead our education and training work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: One piece of that is offering Know Your Rights trainings to anyone who requests it, free of charge, available in multiple languages, vetted by legal practitioners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: Requests have come from across the city's boroughs, from schools, places of worship, or just a group of concerned neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: And at the end of these trainings, a lawyer like myself does a Q&A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: And without fail, someone asks something along the lines of, does knowing our rights matter if ICE won't respect them anyway?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: And we respond honestly that ICE has certainly demonstrated lawless and brutal behavior, but also that knowing our rights empowers us to try to hold them accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: However, that burden should not fall on individual New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: It is the responsibility and indeed the privilege of those who represent us, and these pieces of legislation are a small yet necessary step towards this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: So much of our immigration law is set at a federal level, but I thank the city council for stepping in where they can.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: May we someday see a return to a country without ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lima Nasrati
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Leona Moore-Brave, a U.S. Navy veteran, says she was falsely arrested by NYPD because she is a brown woman. She supports Intros 1077 and 739 to prevent racial profiling and civil detainers without judicial warrants.
chapters.title: Leona Moore-Brave on false arrest and supports 1077/739

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: Good afternoon, New York City and members of the Committee on Immigration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: My name is Leona Moore-Brave, a U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: Navy veteran, Petty Officer 3rd Class, and I'm here representing our community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: I'm testifying in strong support of 1077 and 0739.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: Over a year ago, I was falsely arrested by NYPD simply for being a brown woman, for looking Hispanic during a climate that treated our faces and our names as probable cause.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: I'm an American citizen who served this country, yet because of how I look and my name, I was treated as if my existence was illegal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: The false arrest nearly cost me my life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: It destroyed my reputation, ruined my ability to get back to work, and left lasting damage that I am still fighting to survive today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: When local law enforcement is allowed to profile people, blur the lines with similar immigration enforcement, or act without strict judicial warrants, it is just...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: It isn't justice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: Undocumented immigrants who are targeted, every woman of color, every black and brown New Yorker, and every citizen who looks like a target is put in danger.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: Women of color in this city are routinely dehumanized and presumed guilty until proven innocent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: We cannot allow the NYPD to operate with loopholes that enable racial profiling and civil detainers without a judicial warrant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: Passing Intro 1077 and Intro 0739 is a critical step.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: step to draw a hard line, enforce accountability, and protect our communities from being profiled, detained, and stripped of their dignity and livelihoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: I urge the council to pass these bills immediately.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: Because I have 28 seconds left, I would like to say I ride the two train.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: I go to the Bronx and every day I see people crying.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leona Moore-Brave
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación

utterances.text: Abina Hutchful, Rachel Goldberg.
