chapters.summary: Alexis Kaloyanidis, member of Community Education Council District 30, describes ICE staging at PS280 and the Marble Hill shooting. She says NYCPS guidance is not public and calls for bold action to protect immigrant students and families.
chapters.title: Alexis Kaloyanidis of CEC 30 on ICE near schools

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I will now call Alexis Kaloyanidis.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, council members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: My name is Alexis Kalyanidis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: I live in Jackson Heights, Queens, and serve on the Community Education Council for District 30.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: CEC 30 proudly represents some of the most ethnically diverse neighborhoods in New York City, if not the world.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: On the first day of school, ICE agents abducted a father on Junction Boulevard in front of his child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: This prompted me to draft Resolution 212, urging NYCPS to take stronger action to protect immigrant students and families from ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: The resolution was unanimously co-sponsored by CEC 30 and passed on September 14th.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: Our council then immediately shared the resolution with Chancellor Samuels, the Panel for Educational Policy, the City Council, and the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs with the hopes that the resolution would be adopted as part of the official NYCPS protocol for

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: non-local law enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: Fast forward, on October 3rd, at least a half dozen ICE agents were witnessed staging in the parking lot of PS280 in Jackson Heights, right around the time that two community members were kidnapped down the block.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: I personally learned of the ice sighting in real time as it was happening, and our council immediately contacted the district superintendent and the PS280 principal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: Days later, of course, on October 8th, Oscar Balgal was shot inside his vehicle while his five-year-old child rode in the back seat.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: NYCPS's updated guidance still has not been made public.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: Our families are left unsure if safety measures even exist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: have stopped coming to PTA meetings and school events out of fear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: I've personally comforted the family members of children who were deported from my kids'school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: One of our CEC 30 members in East Elmhurst regularly drives neighbors to school to keep them safe and off the streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: And we try to fill the gaps because we care so deeply about all of our district's children, but we are doing this work without support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: Our schools are uniquely positioned to provide support as they already know our communities and families intimately.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: Project Open Arms is only staffed by two or three people and is woefully inadequate to meet the immediate and often urgent needs of our families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: I am tired of talking to teachers and administrators who want to do more, but feel their hands are tied.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: NYCPS leadership must empower our individual school leaders to act and to do so publicly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: We need more than comic books, required signage, or backpacked flyers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: We need the city and NYCPS to take bold, direct action to protect our students and their families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: I support the proposed legislation, but we still need more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexis Kaloyanidis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: so much.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you as well and I encourage you and other CEC members to stay on the lookout for the council calendar as we discuss Project Open Arms through this committee in the new year.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I will now call on Mario Bruzwan.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Bruzo one.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Mario Bruzzone of the New York Immigration Coalition says ICE enforcement makes the city less safe and burdens Black and brown communities disproportionately. He urges passage of Intros 1077-A and 1078-A and advancement of Intro 209.
chapters.title: Mario Bruzzone of NY Immigration Coalition supports bills

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: I'm Mario Brisoni, representing the New York Immigration Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: We are a statewide coalition of approximately 200 organizations serving immigrant New Yorkers across all five boroughs and across the state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: Through our work with our member organizations, we see firsthand the impact of escalating immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: ICE enforcement is making our city less safe, and those burdens do not fall equally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: Our own research shows that immigrants from Central and South America are approximately a quarter of the state's non-citizen population, but account for 74% of ICE arrests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: Black and brown communities already experience disproportionate policing and involvement in the criminal legal system, and now they're bearing the brunt of aggressive and discriminatory immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: We see how fear of immigration enforcement affects people's daily lives and why strong sanctuary protections matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: People must be able to turn to their local government to report abuse and seek protection without fearing that their interactions with the city will become a pathway to detention or deportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: Sanctuary laws make clear that the city's resources and institutions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: are here to serve New Yorkers, not to facilitate the federal deportation agenda.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: However, recent incidents, including the ice shooting of Bronx residents Oscar Valgal, raised questions about accountability in the role of local police and immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: They also underscore why New York City must strengthen its sanctuary protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: The city should not use its personnel, its resources, or its authority to facilitate ICE's deportation agenda.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: For New Yorkers who come into contact with the NYPD or Department of Corrections, that interaction should not result in them being handed over to ICE without a judicial warrant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: We urge you to pass Intros 1077A and 1078A and to advance Intro 209.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mario Bruzzone
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

chapters.summary: Council staff note that everyone who signed up has testified and invite any missed witnesses to use the sergeant at arms or Zoom raise-hand function. After reading names of registered but absent witnesses, staff announce written testimony can be submitted for 72 hours and adjourn the hearing.
chapters.title: Staff closes public testimony and adjourns hearing

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I, at this time, is that all that was online?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We have now heard from everyone who has signed up to testify.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: If we inadvertently missed anyone who would like to testify in person, please visit the sergeant at arms table and complete a witness slip now.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: If we inadvertently missed anyone who would like to testify virtually, please use the raise hand function in Zoom and a member of our staff will call you in the order of hands raised.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I will now read the names of those who registered to testify but have not yet filled out a witness slip or appeared on Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Anthony Kelzo, Joshua Santiago, Deborah Lee, Ben Broski,

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Adama Ba, Vladimir Tauhi, and Kevin Cho.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Seeing no one else, I would like to note again that written testimony, which will be reviewed in full by committee staff, may be submitted

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: to the record up to 72 hours after the close of this hearing by emailing it to testimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: This hearing is hereby adjourned.

summary: Committee on Immigration holds an oversight hearing on immigration enforcement activity in New York City and four items: Intro 739, Proposed Intro 1077-A, Proposed Intro 1078-A, and Resolution 729.
Administration officials, NYPD, MOIA, advocates, and public witnesses testify on ICE operations, sanctuary law compliance, detainer policies, training, and legal services funding.

Chair Encarnación and council members question NYPD and MOIA about the Marble Hill shooting, NYPD-ICE interactions, DOC transfers, and accountability; public testimony largely supports the Cut Ties with ICE package.
title: Committee on Immigration
topic: Oversight - Examining the Current State of Immigration Enforcement Activity in New York City
